title: ctlv: Add the UAPI wire format and family API
overview: Headers-only patch that fixes the contract of the series: the userspace TLV wire format, ioctl and event record (uapi/linux/ctlv.h), the cursor type shared by core and families (linux/ctlv.h), and the static schema/op/family descriptors that generated family code fills in (linux/ctlv_family.h). Later patches (core, generated *_gen.c, family implementations) all build on these three headers; the ioctl-number and MAINTAINERS edits just register them.

files.purpose: Central registry of ioctl magic numbers; reserves a code for CTLV so it does not collide with other drivers.

units.title: Reserve ioctl magic 0xBB
units.summary: Adds the 0xBB, 00-0F range to uapi/linux/ctlv.h, matching CTLV_IOC_MAGIC.
units.details: The row is placed between 0xBA and 0xC0 in magic order; only sequence 0x00 (CTLV_IOC_OP_EXEC) is used in this series.

files.purpose: Kernel maintainer database; extends the existing CTLV entry to cover the new headers.

units.title: CTLV entry: add header globs
units.summary: Adds include/linux/ctlv*.h and include/uapi/linux/ctlv*.h to the CTLV file patterns.
units.details: The globs also match later generated/family headers such as ctlv_gen.h.

files.purpose: Small in-kernel header exposing the cursor type that family callbacks use to read requests and write replies. Includes the UAPI header; other core types stay opaque via forward declarations.

units.title: Header, includes and forward declarations
units.summary: Include guard, UAPI include and opaque forward declarations of core types.
units.details: Families only hold pointers to ctlv_device, ctlv_family, ctlv_msg, ctlv_op_ctx and ctlv_schema_tree; their layouts are private to the core.

units.title: struct ctlv_cursor
units.summary: A fixed-size handle for one attribute position in one message, used for reading requests and building replies.
units.details:
- Reading uses @attr/@parent; writing uses @start and the @up chain, which forms the stack of open nests.
- @tree/@node/@depth tie the position to the schema so helpers can validate types and nesting.
- Being fixed-size, a family can place child cursors on its stack; members belong to the core and a helper of the wrong direction refuses the cursor.
- Passed to ctlv_action_fn/ctlv_query_fn/ctlv_stub_fill_fn in ctlv_family.h.

files.purpose: Kernel-side API for family implementations and generated code: constant-initialisable schema tables (nodes, stubs, ops, family), op/lifecycle callback types and struct ctlv_family. Generated *_gen.c files build these tables with the macros here; the core consumes them to validate and dispatch.

units.title: Header, includes and nest-depth limit
units.summary: Guard, includes and CTLV_MAX_DECLARED_NEST_DEPTH, one level below the wire limit.
units.details: The spare level is reserved so op-schema-get can wrap a described schema in one extra nest.

units.title: struct ctlv_node_schema
units.summary: One flat schema node: attr ID, kind, unit/scale, occurrence bound, child range and a kind-specific constraint union.
units.details:
- Trees are flat arrays; nests refer to children by @first_child/@children_count, with @required_children_count of them mandatory.
- @reenters marks a nest that may recurse into an ancestor node.
- The union holds range (uint/sint/enum), flags_mask, length (string/binary) or blob parameters, selected by @kind (enum ctlv_schema_kind).
- CTLV_NODE_SCHEMA_UNLIMITED (0) means no occurrence cap.

units.title: Node schema initialiser macros: nest, uint, sint
units.summary: Designated-initialiser helpers that build a ctlv_node_schema for the root, nests and integer/enum attrs.
units.details: The __ forms are the common base; the public forms fix the kind and fill the union member. Used by generated tables.

units.title: Node schema initialiser macros: flags, bool, string, binary, blob
units.summary: Initialisers for the remaining leaf kinds.
units.details: STRING and BINARY share the length union member; BLOB fills max_len, alignment, backings and direction.

units.title: Stub schema and initialisers
units.summary: Describes a placeholder node in a tree whose content is supplied by another family's fill schema.
units.details: Identified by (family_id, set_id) plus the node index; @optional lets the slot be left unfilled.

units.title: struct ctlv_schema_tree and tree macros
units.summary: Bundle of a node array and optional stub array, with macros that build it from a naming convention.
units.details: CTLV_SCHEMA_TREE(name) expects `name_node_schemas`; the _STUBS form also expects `name_stub_schemas`; _NONE gives an empty tree for ops without a request or reply.

units.title: struct ctlv_stub_fill_schema
units.summary: The member tree a family contributes to fill a stub identified by (family_id, set_id).
units.details: CTLV_STUB_FILL_SCHEMA takes `name_fill` as the member tree. It is matched at runtime to stub_ops (ctlv_stub_ops) with the same IDs.

units.title: struct ctlv_op_sizes and struct ctlv_op_schema
units.summary: Per-op size limits and the op descriptor: ID, type, fd access, availability, request and reply trees.
units.details:
- Sizes: request max, action reply max, query reply min/suggested, event record max.
- @type is a CTLV_OP_TYPE_* value (action, query, event) and @availability a CTLV_OP_AVAILABILITY_* value; both come from the family's generated header.
- @pre_post flags ops that have pre/post hooks in the family's op table.

units.title: Op schema initialiser macros
units.summary: Build ctlv_op_schema entries for actions, queries and events, filling the size fields that apply to each type.
units.details: Events have no request, are always CTLV_OP_AVAILABILITY_FIXED and set only event_record_max_len. Extra designated initialisers pass through __VA_ARGS__ (e.g. optional, pre_post).

units.title: struct ctlv_family_schema and uevent limits
units.summary: Static description of one family: name, ID, op schema array and stub fill schemas; plus uevent size budgets.
units.details: The uevent limits keep CTLV to half of UEVENT_BUFFER_SIZE and UEVENT_NUM_ENVP, leaving the rest to the device model.

units.title: struct ctlv_input_ref and op callback types
units.summary: Input reference record, the action/query/pre/post function types, struct ctlv_op and its initialiser macros.
units.details:
- ctlv_op holds either an action or a query handler (union) plus optional pre and post hooks.
- Handlers get the family's private data, the op context, a const request cursor and a reply cursor.
- CTLV_OP_* macros assemble entries from a name prefix: `name_action`, `name_query`, `name_pre`, `name_post`.

units.title: Family lifecycle types and stub ops
units.summary: Family lifecycle callback types and struct ctlv_stub_ops that binds a (family, set) stub to its fill function.
units.details: Lifecycle order is pre_init, init, post_init at device creation and pre_fini, fini at teardown, with priv_size giving the size of the family's private area. ctlv_stub_fill_fn writes the members for a stub into a nest cursor.

units.title: struct ctlv_family and root family
units.summary: The registration object for a family: schema, optional parent, op handler table, family-wide hooks, lifecycle callbacks and stub ops.
units.details: @parent links a derived family to a base family. The extern `ctlv_family` is the root family, defined by the core with the generated ctlv_gen output.

files.purpose: Userspace-visible, schema-free transport definition: TLV attribute header and ID encoding, schema kind and unit enums, the op-execution ioctl, the event record header and implementation limits. Per-family constants live in generated headers.

units.title: Header and struct ctlv_attr
units.summary: License, includes, the 16-byte attribute header and 8-byte alignment macros.
units.details:
- `len` covers header plus payload but not the leaf's own padding; nested payloads concatenate CTLV_ALIGN(child.len) per child.
- attr_id is __aligned_u64 so 32-bit ABIs lay out identically.
- Scalars are native-endian; occurrences of one ID are contiguous within a root or nest.

units.title: Attribute flags and ID encoding
units.anchor: Set exactly on root and nested attrs
units.summary: Flag bits (NESTED, FRAG_MORE, IGNORE_IF_UNKNOWN) and the 64-bit attr and op ID layouts with accessors.
units.details:
- Attr ID: family 63..48, group 47..32, attr 31..0. Op ID: family 63..48, op 31..0.
- CTLV_ATTR_ROOT (0) is valid only at a message start.
- IGNORE_IF_UNKNOWN lets a device skip a request attr whose ID its schema does not declare.

units.title: enum ctlv_unit and enum ctlv_schema_kind
units.summary: Units for integer payloads and the payload forms reported by op-schema-get.
units.details: A payload is value * 10^scale of its unit. Both enums are append-only; kind values index ctlv_node_schema.kind in ctlv_family.h.

units.title: struct ctlv_op_exec and ioctl
units.summary: Argument of CTLV_IOC_OP_EXEC: op ID, request and reply buffers, lengths, and query generation/cursor for fragmented replies.
units.details:
- request/reply are u64 pointers for a compat-identical layout; reply_len is input only.
- generation and cursor are query-only (zero for actions); cursor nonzero resumes a query, and the reply root carries CTLV_ATTR_F_FRAG_MORE when more remains.
- reserved[2] must be zero and provides growth room; the ioctl is _IOWR(0xBB, 0x00).

units.title: struct ctlv_event_hdr
units.summary: Header preceding one root attr in a queued event record returned by read().
units.details: sequence is per open file description and advances on every eligible enqueue attempt, including dropped ones, so readers can detect loss.

units.title: Implementation limits
units.summary: Size and depth limits of this implementation (1 MiB messages, 16 KiB errors, nest depth 32, 64 KiB default query reply, 16 MiB event queue).
units.details: These are not wire-format maxima, so raising them is compatible. CTLV_MAX_NEST_DEPTH feeds CTLV_MAX_DECLARED_NEST_DEPTH in ctlv_family.h.
